ImageDescription.value: The "White House" on the agra site in Markkleeberg, a suburb of Leipzig, Saxony, Germany. It was built in the years 1896/97 by the publisher Paul Herfurth according to the plans of the architect Gustav Hempel. Its architecture is inspired by the "Petit Trianon" in Versailles.

ImageDescription.value: View of the Pickhuben Bridge, the Kleine Fleet, and St. Catherine’s Church in Hamburg from room 402 of the Ameron Hotel on the morning of September 30, 2025. The photograph captures a characteristic urban ensemble of Hamburg’s old port area: the iron Pickhuben Bridge (1887) in the foreground, the narrow canal of the Kleine Fleet lined with brick warehouse buildings from the late 19th century, and the Gothic spire of St. Catherine’s Church, one of the city’s oldest landmarks.

Artist.value: Frank Schulenburg
